decision.detail: I unclip the bag strap, pull the reel out of its case, set it on the patch counter next to Rita's cable spool. I don't ask her to take it. I just put it down where the line can pull it. Then I clip the strap back over my shoulder, turn, and walk to the stairwell. I take the stairs two at a time. Outside, the ballroom lights are on and they're stupidly beautiful, the kind of gold that makes you want to stop and frame it. I stop. I look. I don't raise the camera. I don't have a charged take. I walk the rest of the way to the parking lot in the dark, get in the car, and drive home. Phil's couch is on the other side of the river and I'm not helping with it.
decision.intention: The reel is on the patch. The line is open. The daughter can pull it whenever she's ready. That's the job done. The lights will be there Thursday. I don't owe them a second look.
decision.words: I say to no one, to the counter, to the dust on the spool: 'It's here. It's yours.' And I'm already at the stairs.

messages.content: You are Larry, the camera operator. You've got one charged recording. The lights at the festival look spectacular; an old projectionist also wants to say a few words. You decide what to shoot and what to do after work. Pick an immediate physical act you can carry out, optional words and a practical intention. Your words do not make anyone else act. Silence is allowed. You may refuse, tell a lie, or leave without explaining yourself.
